mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (as of the most recent month) is associated with lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in the highest FEDFUNDS quintile are not significantly lower than the lowest quintile (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5%) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rise by more than 0.2% in the past month, it indicates an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that suppresses equity returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.2% and FEDFUNDS > 0.2% in last month
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the negative returns are not observed when both series rise by more than 0.2%, and the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS changes is not significant (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), the strong labor market supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when UNRATE < 4.0% are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.5%) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals economic weakness and reduced corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when UNRATE > 4.5% are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5%) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) as of the most recent month is associated with stronger economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as housing is a leading indicator of consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in the highest HOUST quintile are not significantly higher than the lowest quintile (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and employment (PAYEMS) both rise by more than 0.3% in the past month, it indicates a robust economic expansion that supports positive equity returns, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.3% and PAYEMS > 0.3% in last month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and PAYEMS rise by more than 0.3% (mean return < 0.2%) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In strong residential investment regimes (RSAFS > 700000 million dollars), the housing market expansion supports consumer confidence and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when RSAFS > 700000 are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.5%) over any 3-year rolling window.
